source: ONS, Crime in England and Wales: Police Force Area data tables, year ending March 2026 (released 23 July 2026), Tables C1, C2 and C5, police recorded crime from the Home Office; rates per 1,000 residents on ONS mid-2025 population estimates
methodology: Counts of police recorded crimes excluding fraud, year ending March 2026, from Table C2, divided by the ONS mid-2025 resident population and multiplied by 1,000. Year on year change is the total in Table C2 against Table C5 (year ending March 2025). Where ONS files several Community Safety Partnerships under one authority, or Cumbria's former districts under their successors, the counts are summed. Where one partnership covers several authorities (Table C1), the partnership's rate is shown on each member and labelled as a partnership figure; nothing is apportioned. Areas whose offences ONS records under an unassigned group, and City of London, are withheld.
denominator: ONS mid-2025 population estimates (Mid-Year Population Estimates, England and Wales, June 2025, published 29 July 2026), taken from src/data/live/population-estimates.json. Mid-2025 (2025-06-30) is the estimate nearest the middle of the year ending March 2026. It comes from the July 2026 series, which revised mid-2022 to mid-2024. ONS's own Table C4 uses mid-2024 population as published before that revision, so rates here differ from C4.
caveat: Police recorded crime is shaped by recording practice, reporting rates and policing priority, and city centre rates are inflated by small resident populations. Offences a force could not place in any area are left out of area figures; each area shows its force's unassigned share.

edition.title: Crime in England and Wales, Police force area data tables - year ending March 2026
edition.releaseDateSource: ONS dataset page at fetch time (data/raw/manifests/ons_pfa_crime.json)

notes.asb: Anti-social behaviour is not in the Police Force Area data tables, so asbRate is blank. No figure is estimated in its place.
notes.hateCrime: Hate crime is not in these tables; hateCrimeCount is blank.
notes.unassigned: ONS CSP note 2: "The number of offences for CSPs for a small number of forces may be lower than the separately published force level totals. Some offences may not have an exact location so it may not be possible to allocate an offence to a CSP, these areas are referred to in the tables as 'Unassigned'. Furthermore, offences in some airports are recorded at the police force area level but are not allocated to a CSP."
notes.kent: ONS CSP note 4: "Due to ongoing IT issues, crime data for Maidstone, Medway, Tonbridge and Malling, Dartford and Gravesham, and Tunbridge Wells are recorded under an unassigned CSP group from 2024 onwards."
notes.derbyshire: ONS CSP note 9: "For the year ending March 2025, data for some areas within Derbyshire have been recorded under an unassigned CSP group. This issue is expected to be corrected for the next publication."
notes.cityOfLondon: ONS CSP note 8: "Rates per 1,000 population are not presented for City of London owing to its small resident population."
notes.sourceAnomaly: In the year ending March 2026 edition some unassigned rows carry a neighbouring force's code; rows are filed to the force block they sit in. See forces[*].rowsFiledUnderAnotherForceCode.

geographyCheck.method: Each area's CSP populations in Table C4 (mid-2024, rounded to 100) are compared with the area's mid-2024 estimate as first published, allowing 50 per CSP for rounding.
